title: What this body keeps (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The specimen in its jar is the one body in the laboratory whose own two controls alter its mechanics, and the hall's whole text is about telling what those controls request from what the body does.
hero.staging: The specimen stood in a column at the north edge and the arrival was an empty slab; the pass restaged the floor (6a2268145). The jar is straight ahead of the arrival with its plate, the formula above and behind it, the four spheres of its terms under the formula, the entropy meter and ceiling at either hand; north of the group the mast and its stand.

plates.title: 1  WHICH STABILITY?
front: The hall opens with a question I would have skipped: which kind of stability am I asking this body to preserve?
I had one word for it. Stable. The jar in front of me needs at least three: it keeps a shape, it keeps moving, it keeps a pressure.
Hold one slider and move the other, the hall says, and watch for long enough.
Long enough is the instruction I am worst at.
One word for three things is how I lose two of them.
back: three floors of rails taught me to read the ends. this one asks me to read the clock.

plates.title: 2  STEADY IS NOT STILL
front: Choose PAIR B. The pressure reading says PULSE. Press PULSE / STEADY and the number settles at its baseline.
Has the body finished moving? Stay with one part of it. It has not.
I stopped the breathing somebody imposed. The specimen remains subject to its other forces.
Steady pressure is something I gave it. Stillness would be something else.
A number that has stopped changing is a fact about the number.
back: on the mast north of here I pressed STEADY and it went on swaying from what had struck it.

plates.title: 3  THREE THINGS TO CHECK
front: LAMBDA asks for stiffness and pressure. PHI asks for damping and drag. That is the intended mapping.
The plate shows numbers. That is the readback. Then there is what the body does.
The hall: the route does not end at the script.
In the engine used here drag is unused, and stiffness changed on a running body does not rebuild its constraints. Pressure and damping do update.
Four requests, two effects. The plate shows four numbers either way.
back: which two took reading the engine. the plate could not have told me.

plates.title: 4  RESISTING IS NOT CALMING
front: Resisting a deformation is different from reducing ongoing motion.
A body can resist changing shape and go on moving. A body can be slowed and still be soft.
I say rigid, or I say fluid, and each word has swallowed both.
The hall asks me to follow one region through several moments, not every moving surface at once.
Two instants can look alike while what happens between them differs.
back: the mast has two dials for it. stiffer: a swing went from 2.12 s to 1.58 s. more damping: 0.53 of a swing left became 0.20.

plates.title: 5  TWO PAIRS, ONE PRESSURE
front: Lambda 0.2 with phi +0.8. Then lambda 0.8 with phi -0.8.
Both give the same steady pressure baseline. Damping differs. The built stiffness stays where it was.
On the pressure reading the two are one setting. In the jar they are not.
Which difference do I notice first? The hall asks me not to reduce both to one word.
Name what changed, not what the interface meant to change.
back: the pressure has a designed peak near the middle, so 0.2 and 0.8 reach the same height from either side. somebody chose that curve.

plates.title: 6  A READBACK IS NOT A CHANGE
front: On the mast I asked for stiffness 16. The stand read back 16. A swing still took 2.12 s.
The spring that was running had been built at 9. Asking did not rebuild it.
After REBUILD: nine rings on the foot, and 1.58 s.
Drag I asked for, and it read back 0.5, and neither figure moved. Nothing uses it.
A property readback alone cannot establish that a running constraint changed. I had been treating the echo as the answer.
back: damping was taken at once: 0.20 of a swing left after one. some asking does work. that is what makes the rest hard to see.

plates.title: 7  THE JAR IS NOT ON THE SLIDERS
front: The name above the glass stays. Inside, the terms of holding together have changed.
The jar supplies terms of its own: a bottom, sides, a lid.
I can watch through it. The specimen cannot leave through it.
The sliders do not move those boundaries. Nothing on the plate does.
Everything I am allowed to vary is inside something I am not.
back: the slab, the storey height, the two shafts: same.

plates.title: 8  KEEP KEEPS THE SETTINGS
front: KEEP preserves settings for this run. Not a recoverable body.
If I set the same numbers tomorrow I make the same requests. The body that answered today is gone.
The hall: a future observation could preserve a trace of deformation over time.
The mast keeps twelve seconds of where its tip was. It is the only record on this floor of what a body did.
A saved setting is a memory of what I asked.
back: twelve seconds is not long. the trace forgets too. it forgets later.

plates.title: 9  WHAT HAVE WE TRAINED OURSELVES TO SEE?
front: A responsive specimen is not an assay of queerness or a test for life. The hall says so.
We gave this body a name, a container and a range of responses.
Then we watched it, and what we learned to recognise was that range.
Which part of the apparatus would we change next? I looked at the sliders first. Then at the jar. Then at the name.
I notice the order I looked in.
back: the floor still promises an imago and a return transformed. the working copy asks for requested settings and supported effects. both are here.

threads.why: Which stability: the first answer the plate offers is a steady number, and that is not stillness.
Which stability: keeping a shape and losing motion are two different things to ask for.
A button changed a number; what it changed in the body is a third thing to check.
Mapping, readback, response: on the mast the third is measured.
Two combinations that one word would cover, and one reading does.
The sliders move pressure and damping; the jar is not on them.
If the readback is an echo, what is kept should be a trace of what the body did.
The container is part of what was given to the body, with the name and the range.
Settings are kept, the body is not: which part of the apparatus would be changed next?

visual_arguments.title: ASKED, READ BACK, MEASURED
visual_arguments.claim: What a control requested, what a property reports and what a body does are three accounts; a request can be read back in full and change nothing; steady is not still; and only a trace kept over time is the body's own account.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'The intended mapping, the number on the plate and the mechanical response are three things we have to check against one another.' ... 'A property readback alone cannot establish that a running constraint changed.' ... 'Steady pressure is something you have given it. Stillness would be something else.'
built_from: a mast three metres tall on a sprung foot, with rings that show the spring as built
six plates: STIFFNESS, REBUILD, DAMPING, DRAG, PULSE, BREATHE / STEADY
a stand with three columns (asked, read back, measured) for three properties
a trace of the tip's place over the last twelve seconds
visual_arguments.what_stands: North of the specimen a thin mast with a violet head on a dark foot wound with orange rings, a row of six pale plates in front of it, a dark stand behind it with a table and a moving trace.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Stand on PULSE and watch the measured column. Stand on STIFFNESS, then PULSE again. Stand on REBUILD, then PULSE. Ask for DAMPING. Ask for DRAG. Press BREATHE / STEADY twice.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: A swing whose time does not change when stiffness is asked for and read back; rings that appear and a shorter swing after REBUILD; a trace that dies sooner with damping; a drag figure nothing uses; a mast still moving after STEADY.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/asked_read_measured_walk.gd, the tower's walker: a swing 2.12 s with 0.43 left after one; stiffness asked and read back 16 while built 9, still 2.12 s; rebuilt, nine rings and 1.58 s; damping 2.0, 0.20 left; drag 0.5, no change; steady and still moving (7 of 7). Not tried in a headset.

open: Plates 2, 3, 5 and 7 repeat what the hall text says the specimen does (PAIR B, the engine's unused drag, the two combinations, the jar); the pass read the specimen's code and did not measure the soft body in the running tower.
The mast is not the specimen: it shows the three accounts on a spring computed in this script, with a REBUILD plate the specimen does not have. Plate 6 says 'on the mast'.
The formula, the four spheres, the entropy meter, the entropy ceiling and the grasp cabinet on this floor are not mentioned in the hall text and carry no plate.
The tower's timeline walk still paints its stops where this floor's works stood before the restaging; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

threads.why: Which stability: there are at least three, and one word loses two of them.
A steady pressure is a number that stopped changing; that is a fact about the number.
Mapping, readback, response: counted, four requests and two effects.
Drag is unused and built stiffness is not rebuilt: the two requests with no effect.
A body can resist and still move; rigid and fluid each swallow both.
A readback alone establishes nothing about the running body: it is an echo.
The same pressure baseline with different damping: one setting on the reading, two in the jar.
Naming what changed, not what was intended, is what the one word prevents.
The sliders do not move the jar: what may be varied is inside what may not.
KEEP preserves settings, not a body: a memory of what was asked.
Not an assay and not a test for life: then what was being looked for, and in what order?
What we trained ourselves to recognise shows in the order of looking: sliders, then jar, then name.
